newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra hopeful on labour reform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra hopeful on labour reform.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations minister Peter Reith said on Saturday he was confident that guarantees of voluntary unionism in his proposed industrial relations law would survive parliament.
He also said he expected the new industrial relations system to begin in early 1997.

"On the basis of publicly-reported remarks of the Democrats, I am confident about the likely outcome in respect of the bill on voluntary unionism," Reith told a conference of the ruling Liberal Party.

The government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate, the upper house of parliament. All other groups in the Senate, except the seven-strong Australian Democrats and perhaps one independent senator, are opposed to Reith's bill.
Reith is negotiating with the Democrats for the passage of the new system, which -- among many changes -- would inject more competition into industrial relations and reduce union power.
Reith said that since the bill would soon enter the tortuous committee stage of the senate process, it should be enacted by the end of the year when the current session of parliament ends.

"What that means is that we're basically on track to see the completion of the legislation during this session and the commencement of a new industrial relations system for Australia early in 1997," he said.
